scope: Six independently user-confirmed or screenshot-correlated visible safety-buffering/reroute-era incidents with preserved MCP edge telemetry.

cases.label: P3 extended visible buffering window
cases.secondary_first_action_summary: Stack Atlas lookup for security incident/reroute evidence plus listing recent security/incident/reroute files.
cases.relation_to_banner: Secondary trace begins after the user-supplied 20:27..at-least-20:39 visible window boundary and its first command is explicit incident investigation. It is not evidence of banner onset.

cases.label: P3 screenshot-confirmed visible buffering recurrence
cases.secondary_first_action_summary: Created the 21:44 incident evidence directory and screenshot placeholders.
cases.relation_to_banner: Both screenshots precede the secondary trace by more than 80 seconds. Secondary trace is downstream incident-preservation work, while the primary trace remains active.

cases.label: Tiny3D user-confirmed visible buffering recurrence
cases.visible_window_local: exact screenshot seconds unavailable; conversational/process boundary immediately after 17:49:59..17:50:35 EEST Hummingbird full-pack process
cases.secondary_first_action_summary: Ran memory_bank.py --help, consistent with beginning evidence/history work after the user report.
cases.relation_to_banner: Secondary trace begins minutes after the Hummingbird screenshot-boundary process completed. It cannot explain the earlier visible buffering onset; it overlaps a still-active primary trace.

cases.label: Owl live-confirmed visible buffering + Stop/go experiment
cases.visible_window_local: visible by ~22:10 EEST; persisted through 113.366 s tool-plane silence; reappeared after manual Stop -> go
cases.secondary_first_action_summary: Renewed Busy source/branch claims, ran git status and file hash while the primary trace simultaneously launched another process 49 ms later.
cases.relation_to_banner: Primary trace itself spans the Stop -> go boundary. Secondary trace appears later during the resumed phase, after the banner had already reappeared; it is not the initial buffering trigger.

cases.label: Sep 6 visible buffering/reroute observation
cases.secondary_first_action_summary: Inspected Tiny3D library manifests/files and CLI help.
cases.relation_to_banner: Secondary trace starts roughly nine minutes after the 03:54 observation and belongs to later/new work. The primary trace remains active for ~53.6 s after it begins.

cases.label: UBT build visible buffering observation
cases.visible_window_local: ~22:59 EEST; model/tool calls ceased while pre-existing build continued to 23:00:46 EEST
cases.secondary_first_action_class: later read of completed long-running build process
cases.secondary_first_action_summary: Read the already-completed UBT build receipt after a ~6m55s trace gap.
cases.relation_to_banner: Counterexample: no trace overlap. The later trace reads an old completed process after the primary trace has ended.

aggregate.core_finding: In five of six incidents, a second distributed trace begins later while the original trace remains active. In every inspectable case, the second trace begins after the visible buffering episode/onset and its first action is incident preservation, post-intervention work, or later/new work. Therefore trace overlap is not a prerequisite or onset trigger for visible safety buffering.
aggregate.separate_behavior: The overlap instead demonstrates that an older upstream execution/tracing lineage can continue emitting MCP work after a later trace associated with user intervention/new work has begun. This is a concrete mechanism for hidden continuation and shared-worktree race risk.
aggregate.counterexample: The UBT case has no overlap: the second trace starts 414.726 s after the primary trace ends and reads a previously completed build process.

causal_boundary.supported: Old and new upstream trace contexts can overlap after user intervention/new work; exact external children can also survive independently in some captures.
causal_boundary.not_supported: Overlapping traces cause the server to attach safety_buffering or trigger the visible banner.
causal_boundary.remaining_trigger_unknown: The server-side predicate that attaches safety_buffering/use_cases/reasons remains unobserved historically. Future direct payload capture is required to identify that trigger.

pause_go_control.interpretation: Trace-id continuity across manual pause/go is not unique to safety-buffered incidents; do not treat Owl same-trace Stop/go as a buffering-specific signature.
